Interface RenderContext

All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultRenderContext
public interface RenderContext
Context provided during rendering, giving access to focus state and CSS styling.

This interface exposes only what user code needs during rendering. Internal framework functionality is handled automatically.

    • resolveStyle

      default Optional<CssStyleResolver> resolveStyle(Styleable element)
      Resolves the CSS style for an element.

      Returns the resolved CSS style if a StyleEngine is configured and matching rules are found, or empty if no CSS styling is applicable.

      Parameters:
      element - the element to resolve styles for
      Returns:
      the resolved style, or empty if no CSS is applicable

    • resolveStyle

      default Optional<CssStyleResolver> resolveStyle(String styleType, String... cssClasses)
      Resolves the CSS style for a virtual element with the given type and classes.

      This is useful for resolving styles for sub-elements (like list items) that aren't full Element instances but need CSS styling.

      Parameters:
      styleType - the element type (e.g., "ListItem")
      cssClasses - the CSS classes to apply
      Returns:
      the resolved style, or empty if no CSS is applicable

    • parseColor

      default Optional<Color> parseColor(String colorValue)
      Parses a CSS color value string into a Color.

      Supports named colors (e.g., "red", "blue"), hex colors (e.g., "#ff0000"), and RGB notation (e.g., "rgb(255,0,0)").

      Parameters:
      colorValue - the CSS color value string
      Returns:
      the parsed color, or empty if parsing fails

    • currentStyle

      default Style currentStyle()
      Returns the current style from the style stack.

      This style represents the accumulated styles from parent elements and should be used as the base for rendering operations.

      Returns:
      the current style, or Style.EMPTY if no style is active

    • childStyle

      default Style childStyle(String childName)
      Resolves CSS style for a child element.

      The child type is derived from the current element's type plus the child name (e.g., for a ListElement rendering, "item" becomes "ListElement-item").

      Example usage: 

      Style itemStyle = context.childStyle("item");
Style selectedStyle = context.childStyle("item", PseudoClassState.ofSelected());

      This enables CSS selectors like: 

      ListElement-item { color: white; }
ListElement-item:selected { color: cyan; text-style: bold; }
#nav ListElement ListElement-item:selected { color: green; }
      Parameters:
      childName - the child name (e.g., "item", "header", "tab")
      Returns:
      the resolved style, merged with the current context style

    • childStyle

      default Style childStyle(String childName, PseudoClassState state)
      Resolves CSS style for a child element with a pseudo-class state.

      Use this for stateful children like selected items or focused tabs.

      Parameters:
      childName - the child name (e.g., "item", "row", "tab")
      state - the pseudo-class state (e.g., selected, hover, disabled)
      Returns:
      the resolved style, merged with the current context style

    • childStyle

      default Style childStyle(String childName, ChildPosition position)
      Resolves CSS style for a child element at a specific position.

      The position enables CSS pseudo-class matching for :first-child, :last-child, and :nth-child(even/odd).

      Example usage: 

      for (int i = 0; i < rows.size(); i++) {
    ChildPosition pos = ChildPosition.of(i, rows.size());
    Style rowStyle = context.childStyle("row", pos);
    // CSS can now match :first-child, :last-child, :nth-child(even), etc.
}
      Parameters:
      childName - the child name (e.g., "row", "cell")
      position - the position of the child within its siblings
      Returns:
      the resolved style, merged with the current context style

    • childStyle

      default Style childStyle(String childName, ChildPosition position, PseudoClassState state)
      Resolves CSS style for a child element at a specific position with additional state.

      Combines positional pseudo-classes (:first-child, :last-child, :nth-child) with state pseudo-classes (:selected, :hover).

      Example usage: 

      for (int i = 0; i < rows.size(); i++) {
    ChildPosition pos = ChildPosition.of(i, rows.size());
    boolean isSelected = (i == selectedIndex);
    PseudoClassState state = isSelected ? PseudoClassState.ofSelected() : PseudoClassState.NONE;
    Style rowStyle = context.childStyle("row", pos, state);
}
      Parameters:
      childName - the child name (e.g., "row", "cell")
      position - the position of the child within its siblings
      state - additional pseudo-class state (e.g., selected, hover)
      Returns:
      the resolved style, merged with the current context style

    • renderChild

      default void renderChild(Element child, Frame frame, Rect area)
      Renders a child element within the given area.

      Container elements should use this method instead of calling child.render() directly. This allows the infrastructure to handle errors gracefully when fault-tolerant mode is enabled, and ensures that all rendered elements are properly registered with the event router, enabling them to receive key and mouse events.

      Example usage in a container element: 

      for (Element child : children) {
    context.renderChild(child, frame, childArea);
}
      Parameters:
      child - the child element to render
      frame - the frame to render into
      area - the area allocated for the child
